articles.title: Cyclone Murasu Set to Trigger Heavy Rain, Winds in Odisha; IMD Issues Orange Alert - Pragativadi

articles.full_text:
As Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu advances towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, several parts of Odisha are bracing for severe weather disruptions.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast torrential rain, active thunderstorms, and strong squally winds across multiple districts in the state.
Heavy Rainfall Warning for Ganjam and Gajapati
According to the latest meteorological bulletins, isolated heavy rainfall is expected to lash the Gajapati and Ganjam districts starting today. The severe weather activity will be accompanied by lightning and gusty winds reaching speeds of 40 to 50 kmph, with peak gusts touching 60 kmph in several coastal and southern districts.
The affected regions subject to high-wind and thunderstorm warnings include:
-
Southern & Coastal Belt: Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati, Ganjam, Puri, and Khordha.
-
Central & Northern Districts: Baleswar, Bhadrak, Jajpur, Kendrapada, Jagatsinghpur, Kataka, Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj, Kalahandi, Kandhamala, Nabarangpur, and Nayagada (experiencing winds up to 30–40 kmph gusting to 50 kmph).
Nowcast Advisory Issued for 10 Districts
In a short-range nowcast warning issued early today, the Met Department flagged 10 districts for immediate weather activity. Light to moderate rain, together with isolated thunder and lightning, is expected over Baleshwar, Bhadrak, Kendrapada, Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, and Malkangiri.
Residents in these zones are strongly advised to limit unnecessary travel, stay updated on local weather developments, and seek safe shelter during periods of heavy lightning.
Orange Warning Extended for South Odisha
The IMD has escalated warnings for South Odisha by issuing an Orange Alert covering November 3 and November 4. During this window, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati, and Ganjam are likely to experience heavy to very heavy downpours. Wind speeds across the region are expected to intensify to 50–60 kmph, with gusts up to 70 kmph.
Flood and Landslide Threats
Authorities have cautioned that sustained heavy rain over the coming 48 hours could lead to local flood-like conditions and severe waterlogging in low-lying urban and rural areas. In hilly terrains—particularly across Gajapati, Koraput, and Rayagada—the risk of landslides remains high. Local administrations have been put on high alert to handle emergencies, manage drainage blockages, and ensure swift evacuation if water levels rise.

The stratospheric polar vortex is weakening much earlier than usual; forecasts indicate a reversal of the westerly winds in early November. In practice, the winds in the stratosphere that circle the North Pole, blowing from west to east, could slow down to the point where they change direction and start blowing from east to west.
At this time of year, this is very rare, as the polar vortex usually tends to strengthen. The earliest inversion event on record was in late November 1968.

This is written by atmospheric physicist Francesco Nucera, a meteorologist at 3bmeteo since 2008: “The stratospheric polar vortex is a large circulation of winds that forms over the Arctic, at an altitude of approximately 30 kilometres. It is a very long way from the ground, yet it can interact with the circulation closer to the surface – the one that determines the weather at our latitudes. But a
Lower temperatures
“Since the Halloween and All Saints’ Day weekend, there has been a shift across the hemisphere, with cold air masses arriving directly from the area between Finland and western Russia, moving southwards towards the Mediterranean basin.
This cold spell has led to a drop in temperatures across much of Italia: whilst it is not extremely cold, temperatures are a few degrees below the climatological average; this has been exacerbated by biting winds from the north.
Loading...
So says Mattia Gussoni, a meteorologist at ilMeteo.it.
“The bad weather really set in during the course of Sunday 1 November (All Saints’ Day). The influx of cold air over the Mediterranean will encourage the formation of a low-pressure system. This low-pressure vortex,” continues Gussoni, “will trigger thunderstorms that are particularly active, fuelled by the energy accumulated from a Mediterranean Sea that is still mild (warmer-than-average waters will result in higher humidity in the lower layers and a surplus of potential energy).”
The weather systems are affecting Romagna, Marche, Abruzzo, Molise, Puglia, Campania, Calabria, Sardinia and Sicily, with rainfall totals locally reaching up to 50–60 millimetres within a few hours, particularly along the Adriatic coast. The weather is more stable across the rest of Italia, albeit in rather cool conditions.”
“The drop in temperature will also bring snow back to the Apennine mountain range.
In the central-southern Apennines, snowflakes fell as low as 800–1,000 metres, particularly between Sunday evening and the early hours of Monday, blanketing the inland areas of the Marche, Abruzzo, Molise and Lazio, whilst in the remaining southern mountains the snow line will be at higher altitudes. Some snowfall is also expected in the central-eastern Alps, generally above 1,000 metres. These conditions of marked atmospheric activity and decidedly cold weather will persist into the start of next week, with precipitation continuing to affect the central and southern regions in particular,” concludes Gussoni.

Civil Protection: orange alert in Puglia and Basilicata
A low-pressure system, moving down from the Balkans towards the Tyrrhenian Sea, is causing unsettled conditions in central and southern Italy, with scattered showers and thunderstorms. On 2 November, the deepening of the low-pressure system over the southern Tyrrhenian Sea is causing a marked deterioration in conditions along the central Adriatic coast and across much of the south, with widespread rainfall – including thunderstorms and heavy downpours – accompanied by a general increase in wind speeds.
On the basis of the available forecasts, the Department of Civil Protection, in consultation with the regions concerned – which are responsible for activating civil protection systems in the affected areas – has issued a new advisory on adverse weather conditions. These weather events, affecting various parts of the country, could lead to hydrogeological and hydraulic risks, which are summarised in a national overview in the national risk and alert bulletin available on the Department’s website.
The forecast predicts, from the early hours of today, 2 November, scattered to widespread rainfall – including showers and thunderstorms – over Abruzzo, Molise and Sicily, extending to Campania, Calabria, Puglia and Basilicata, with persistent rainfall in the latter and along the eastern Apennine slopes of Abruzzo and Molise.
These conditions will be accompanied by heavy showers, strong gusts of wind, localised hailstorms and frequent lightning. Furthermore, from early tomorrow morning, strong to gale-force northerly winds are forecast for Lazio, particularly in the northern areas, Campania and Sicily, with strong gale-force gusts in the southern parts of the island, subsequently extending and veering from the east towards Basilicata and Puglia.
Based on the forecast conditions, the following has been assessed for today, Monday 2 November: an orange alert has been issued for today, Monday 2 November, due to meteorological and hydrogeological risk in Puglia and Basilicata. A yellow alert is in place in Calabria, Campania, Molise, Abruzzo and Sicily.
